full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J : This Rule at the instance of the defendant petitioner call in question the legality and propriety of the order No. 22 dated 28.9.93 passed by the Assistant Judge, Biswanath, Sylhet rejecting the prayer of the petitioner for examining the opposite party by a-Gynecologist in Family Case No. 2 of 1993 and also rejecting the prayer of the defendant petitioner to allow him to co habit with his wife for one year. 

 2. The case of the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 is that on 10.8.1991 the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 got married with defendant petitioner and dower was fixed at Taka 1,00000/- on 6.9.91 the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 went to the house of the defendant petitioner for starting conjugal life and then the plaintiff opposite party realised that the defendant petitioner is in capable of leading a married life as he is impotent. The plaintiff opposite party no. 1 wanted to divorce and approached the defendant petitioner and his relatives but the defendant petitioner refused to divorce the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 on 6.3.93, Since the defendant petitioner failed to perform his marital obligation the plaintiff opposite party claimed half of prompt dower and half of deafened dower from the defendant petitioner. The defendant petitioner failed to pay same and subsequently the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 filed a suit being Family Suit No. 3 of 1993 before the Assistant Judge, Biswannath, Sylhet. 

 3. The defendant petitioner contested the suit by filing the written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint and contending, inter alia, that both the parties lived together for one month as husband and wife and after one month the father of the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 came and took away the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 for one week. After one week when the defendant petitioner went to his father in law's house to bring his wife, father-in-law refused to give his daughter back the uncle of the defendant quarreled with the father in law over a sum of money taken as loan. The defendant petitioner tried to bring his wife and approached the relation and the plaintiff opposite party herself wants to come back to the defendant petitioner as they were leading a happy married life. But the father of the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 compelled the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 to file the present case on false and concocted allegations against the defendant petitioner. 

 4. The defendant petitioner also filed a case against the plaintiff opposite party before the said family court for restitution of the conjugal life which is numbered as Family Case No. 7 of 1993. The said suit is pending for disposal. 

 5. The present suit namely family case no. 2 of 1993 came up for peremptory hearing and after completion of the evidence of both sides the defendant petitioner filed two applications before the family court on 25.9.93. By the first application the defendant petitioner wanted to get the plaintiff opposite party examined by a Gynecologist to ascertain whether she is Virgo intact (virgin) as alleged by the plaintiff opposite party and by the second application the defendant petitioner also prayed for allowing him to co habit with the plaintiff opposite party for one year to controvert the Staten’s made by the plaintiff opposite party no. 1 in there plaint of the instant suit. The learned family court by order dated 28.9.1993 rejected the said applications and being aggrieved by the said order the defendant petitioner obtained the present Rule. 

 6. Mrs. Salma Masud Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant petitioner, submits that the order of the family court is neither proper nor in accordance with law and further more the impugned order has been passed without considering the facts and circumstances of the case and consequently has caused miscarriage of justice. The learned Advocate further suits that the family court committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in its decision in failing to consider that for ends of justice and for adjudication of the case the learned Judge ought to have ordered for examining the plaintiff by a Gynecologist to ascertain whether she is virgin as alleged by the plaintiff and also allowed the defendant to go to the plaintiff opposite party to controvert the false allegations as leveled against him in the plaint. 

 7. Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 submits that the family court rightly rejected the application of the defendant petitioner by taking correct view of law in as much as the observation of the family court that the onus is on each party prove his own case is absolutely correct and as such after closing of the evidence of both the sides such application cannot be entertained particularly in view of the fact that it is the responsibility of the plaintiff to prove her own case and she will only win if he an substantiate her allegation before the court by cogent evidence and she will not get the decree at the weakness of the adversey and in that view of law the rejection of the first application by the family court cannot be assailed on any ground whatsoever. Mr. Chowdhury next submits that in rejecting the second application the family court took a correct view of law in as such as admittedly the defendant petitioner has field another suit in the self same family court being family case No. 7 of 1993 for restitution of conjugal rights and in that case the onus is on him to prove his case and if he can discharge his onus by producing cogent evidence he will get decree from the court in his favour and in the instant case that he is not physically incapable in discharging marital obligations and as such the onus is on him to prove his defence case and in that view of the matter he should examine himself by a competent doctor to prove that he is not impotent but instead of doing so he went to gel the plaintiff examined by Gynecologist which cannot be entertained. 

 8. on a Perusal of the impugned order it appears both the sides have adduced their evidence in- support of their respective cases and when the date is fixed for argument the defendant petitioner filed two applications on 25. 9. 93, one for examining the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 by a Gynecologist to see whether she is still virgin and by the second application of the same date the defendant petitioner sought for permission of the family court to allow him to co habit with the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 for one year so as to enable him to prove that he is not physically incapable of discharging his marital obligations. It is apparent from the impugned order that the family court rejected the first application on the ground that the onus in on a party to prove his own case by adducing necessary evidence before the trial court and in the instant case both the parties have adduced their evidence in support of their respective cases and since the application filed by the defendant petitioner to ascertain the virginity of the plaintiff opposite party cannot be entertained in view of the fact that in the instant case the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 is to prove her case and will get its own course and for that matter she cannot be 

 examined by a competent doctor to ascertain as to whether she is virgin or not because thereby the onus of proving the defence will be illegally shifted on the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 and in that view of the matter the learned family court correctly appreciated the legal aspect of the case and rightly rejected the first application of the defendant petitioner. 

 9. The learned Family court rejected the second application of the defendant petitioner on the ground that the defendant petitioner without examining himself by a competent doctor he wants to get the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 examined by a doctor. In rejecting the said application the learned family court observed that the allegations against the defendant petitioner is that he is impotent and to rebut the said allegation the defendant petitioner instead of choosing himself to be examined by a doctor wants to get the opposite party No. 1 examined by a Gynecologist which is nothing but an unholy attempt on the part of the defendant petitioner to get the benefit indirectly which he cannot get directly. It appears to me that the learned family court after taking into consideration all the relevant facts and circumstance of the case and after correctly appreciating the legal aspect of the case rejected the second application of cogent and valid ground. In passing the impugned order the learned family court has not committed any illegality whatsoever. In my opinion the impugned order does not suffer from any illegality or infirmity which calls for interference by this 'court and in that view of the matter the revisional application must be rejected as do not find any substance in it.
